label: input token n at original position >= 3
explanation: Token detector for the letter n during the original (input) phase, gated by position: it never fires at positions 0-2, fires weakly and often not at all at position 3 (most false positives are n at t=3), and fires reliably (~3.3% of original steps, i.e. on essentially every n) from position 4 on. Activation magnitude rises with position: low-quartile examples are n at t=3, the top activations are n at position 7-8 (rel ~1.0). Does not fire on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (only a handful of weak activations on n fed back late in the copy phase). Repeated vs first occurrence and the surrounding tokens have little effect.

issues: I upheld the claims after checking. The dev profile shows 0 activations at t=0-2, none on the delimiter, and 38 weak copy-phase activations (at recall_idx 5-8 and t>=14, so late in the copy). Essentially all activation mass is on in_tok n (n: 50496 active, every other token at most 2).

Magnitude rising with position also checks out. t=3 has 9116 activations but holds only 1.2% of the mass. t=8 has 2708 activations and holds 10.4%, so the average activation is much larger late in the sequence.
From orig_idx 4 onward, about 3.3% of steps are active at every position, which matches n's base rate. (in_tok==n)&(phase==0)&(t>=4) scores precision 1.0 and recall 0.818, as the explanation says.

All the false positives sit at t=3. On test, the predicate gives 7142 false positives at t=3; the t==3 predicate alone has precision 0.56. I looked for a clean rule behind which t=3 n's fire and found none. L>=7 vs L<=5 gives 0.55-0.56, vowels have no effect, and in_first gives 0.53. Some history shifts the odds: an earlier n gives 0.85, n as first token 0.89, two or more digits seen 0.78. These are small, graded subsets, so this looks like a threshold effect, not a separate class of counterexamples.
There are 53 test misses, holding 0.0% of the activation mass: tiny copy-phase blips and a few late copy-phase n's. This is scattered noise.
The label says 'position >= 3', which slightly overstates t=3, where the feature fires on only about half of n's. The explanation discloses this, so it is acceptable.
